from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Convolution is a sliding window transformation.", "The kernel is a small mask.", "It scans across the input grid."]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Grid
        input_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.7) for _ in range(16)])
        input_grid.arrange_in_grid(4, 4, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(input_grid, "B1", "E4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(input_grid)
        
        # Setup Kernel Window
        kernel_window = Square(side_length=1.4, color=YELLOW)
        kernel_window.move_to(input_grid[0].get_center() + np.array([0.35, -0.35, 0]))
        self.add(kernel_window)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(kernel_window.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.7))
        self.play(kernel_window.animate.shift(DOWN*0.7))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        kernel_highlight = SurroundingRectangle(input_grid[5:7], color=BLUE, buff=0)
        self.add(kernel_highlight)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(kernel_window.animate.shift(RIGHT*1.4), run_time=2)
        self.remove(kernel_highlight)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Mechanics: The Dot Product Flip", 
                          ["First, we flip the kernel.", "Next, overlay on the input.", "Multiply and sum the values."])
        
        # Elements
        input_vec = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.6, fill_opacity=0.5, color=BLUE) for _ in range(3)])
        input_vec.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        input_text = VGroup(*[Text(str(i+1), font_size=20) for i in range(3)])
        for sq, txt in zip(input_vec, input_text):
            txt.move_to(sq.get_center())
            
        kernel_vec = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.6, fill_opacity=0.5, color=YELLOW) for _ in range(2)])
        kernel_vec.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        kernel_text = VGroup(*[Text("0.5", font_size=18) for _ in range(2)])
        for sq, txt in zip(kernel_vec, kernel_text):
            txt.move_to(sq.get_center())

        input_group = VGroup(input_vec, input_text)
        kernel_group = VGroup(kernel_vec, kernel_text)

        self.place_at_grid(input_group, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(kernel_group, 'D2', scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(kernel_group.animate.rotate(PI))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(kernel_group.animate.move_to(input_group.get_center() + DOWN*0.8))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Sliding animation demo
        self.play(kernel_group.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.7), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Convolutions connect to system memory.", "They process historical inputs.", "Inputs affect the current system state."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Alignment: Why we use Convolutions", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Animate transition from linear transformation to convolution.
        line1_color = "#FFD700"  # Gold
        self.lecture[0].set_color(line1_color)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5)
        square = Square(side_length=1.0, color=RED).set_fill(RED, opacity=0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "B2")
        self.play(FadeIn(circle))
        self.play(Transform(circle, square))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show shift-invariance property visually with a moving pattern.
        line2_color = "#00FF7F"  # SpringGreen
        self.lecture[1].set_color(line2_color)
        
        row_pattern = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.4, color=WHITE).set_fill(GRAY, opacity=0.3) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(row_pattern, "D1", "D4")
        
        pointer = Triangle(color=YELLOW).scale(0.2).rotate(PI)
        self.place_at_grid(pointer, "C2")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(row_pattern), FadeIn(pointer))
        self.play(pointer.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.5), run_time=1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display how convolution reuses weights across the input.
        line3_color = "#87CEFA"  # LightSkyBlue
        self.lecture[2].set_color(line3_color)
        
        label = Text("Weights Reused", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "F3")
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Kernels can extract specific features.", "Edge detection highlights sharp transitions.", "Smoothing filters reduce image noise."]
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Feature Extraction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visuals
        # Represent the Kernel (3x3)
        kernel = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color=BLUE) for _ in range(9)]).arrange_in_grid(rows=3, cols=3, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(kernel, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        kernel_label = Text("Sobel Kernel", font_size=20, color=BLUE).next_to(kernel, UP)
        
        # Represent the image area
        image_area = Rectangle(width=3, height=3, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(image_area, 'E4', scale_factor=1.0)
        image_label = Text("Image Input", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(image_area, UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE), Create(kernel), Write(kernel_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW), Create(image_area), Write(image_label))
        
        # Slide filter across image
        self.play(kernel.animate.move_to(image_area.get_center()), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        feature_map = Square(side_length=1, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(feature_map, 'E6', scale_factor=1.0)
        feature_label = Text("Edges Detected", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(feature_map, DOWN)
        self.play(FadeIn(feature_map), Write(feature_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Convolution is sliding, multiplying, summing.",
            "It is core to CNNs.",
            "It drives digital signal processing."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Conclusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        input_matrix = Matrix([[1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 0], [1, 0, 1]], v_buff=0.3, h_buff=0.3).scale(0.5)
        kernel = Matrix([[0, 1, 0], [1, 1, 1], [0, 1, 0]], v_buff=0.3, h_buff=0.3).scale(0.4)
        output_matrix = Matrix([[0, 0, 0], [0, 5, 0], [0, 0, 0]], v_buff=0.3, h_buff=0.3).scale(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(input_matrix, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(kernel, 'B4')
        self.play(FadeIn(input_matrix), FadeIn(kernel))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(output_matrix, 'E3')
        self.play(FadeIn(output_matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(
            Indicate(input_matrix),
            Indicate(kernel),
            Indicate(output_matrix)
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Signal Processing

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept
sections.content: Define convolution as a sliding transformation. Introduce the 'Kernel' (filter) as a small, weighted mask that scans across an input grid to produce a new output value.
sections.example: Imagine a 3x3 'blurring' filter moving across a photo of a cute Golden Retriever; each position calculates the average intensity of the surrounding pixels to soften the edges.

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics: The Dot Product Flip
sections.content: Explain the step-by-step process: Flip the kernel (mathematical convention), overlay it on the input, perform element-wise multiplication, and sum the results. Visual aid: A 2D grid animation showing the overlapping summation.
sections.example: Representing a signal as a 1D sequence [1, 2, 3] and a kernel [0.5, 0.5]; slide the kernel across to see how the 'weighted moving average' transforms the signal.

sections.title: Prerequisite Alignment: Why we use Convolutions
sections.content: Briefly connect convolution to Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems. Explain that it captures the 'memory' of a system—how an output is affected by a sequence of historical inputs.
sections.example: A robotic arm (system) receiving a stream of velocity commands; the convolution determines the arm's precise current position based on the history of all previous movements.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Feature Extraction
sections.content: Show how different kernels extract specific features. Edge detection kernels highlight transitions (high contrast), while smoothing kernels reduce noise.
sections.example: A security camera system using a 'Sobel filter' kernel to instantly detect the sharp edges of an intruder moving in the dark.

sections.title: Summary & Conclusion
sections.content: Recap the 'Sliding, Multiplying, Summing' workflow. Emphasize that convolution is the backbone of modern Deep Learning (CNNs) and digital signal processing.
sections.example: Final visual: A composite graphic showing a raw image input, a kernel transformation, and the final feature map output—'From pixels to intelligence'.
